newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Lili picks up speed, heads for Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Lili picks up speed, heads for Cuba.

text.p: Hurricane Lili picked up speed as it moved through the northwestern Caribbean toward Cuba Thursday, National Hurricane Center said.

After drifting and stalling for hours during the previous day, the storm's winds climbed to hurricane strength and it took up a northeast track that was expected to take in ashore in Cuba within 24 hours.
At 0800 EDT/1200 GMT, Lili's center was at latitude 19.6 north, longitude 83.4 west, about 260 miles (415 km) south-southwest of Havana.
The storm, packing winds of 75 mph (120 kph), was moving north-northeast at about eight mph (13 kph) and was expected to continue on that track for the next 24 hours.

A hurricane warning was in effect for Cuba's western provinces of Pinar del Rio, Havana, Matanzas, Villa Clara and Cienfuegos, and the Isle of Youth. Forecasters said the warning could be extended eastward through Cuba later Thursday.
A tropical storm warning and hurricane watch were in effect for the Cayman Islands, and small craft in the Florida Keys should stay in port, forecasters said.
On its current track, the center of Lili was expected to approach the south Cuba coast late Thursday or early Friday.
Hurricane-force winds extended 30 miles (50 km) from the center and tropical storm-force winds extended outward up to 140 miles (220 km).
Rainfall up to 12 inches (30 cm) was likely over Cuba and parts of Central America, raising the possibility of deadly flash floods and mud slides in mountainous areas.
